title: Annotatio V §.IV SECOND genus: Christ as eater; spiritual modes differ; impenitent excluded only for spiritual
pass_a_gloss: The SECOND GENUS of Arguments sets forth double eaters hostile and adverse to the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body in the Supper: On one side the Lord Christ commanding to eat, who also Himself ate — gathered by ready enough consequence from Matt. 26:29, Mark 14:24–25, and Luke 22:15–16, the Fathers agreeing (Jerome to Hedibia Q. 2; Augustine On Christian Doctrine 2.3; Chrysostom Hom. 83 on Matt.). But that Christ ate His own Body Oraliter is absurd under many names — see Burmann Disput. XVII on the Supper n. 104. You will say: no less absurd that Christ ate His Body spiritually. Resp. The spiritual mode of eating Christ’s Body is expressly handed down in Scripture, John 6 — not likewise the Oral, about which there is deep silence in Scripture, although eating itself as to the thing and absolutely is read enjoined in express words in the Sacred Supper’s Institution. (2) The spiritual mode of eating Christ’s Body can be various — one fitting Christ, another us; Not likewise the Oral, everywhere as to the thing one and the same by whoever it is performed. Christ spiritually ate His crucified Body, or to-be-crucified inasmuch as to be crucified, by communicating Himself, His passion and death to us and assigning and imputing their fruit and efficacy; We spiritually eat Christ’s Body by embracing Him whole with all His merits by true living faith — i.e. becoming partakers of them. On the other side, those commanded to eat — i.e. converts to the Christian faith, that hence even today all Unbelievers are kept from participation of the Sacred Supper; and indeed such Converts who prove themselves, i.e. who stand in the State of penitence and habit of living faith, the impenitent and impious excluded (1 Cor. 11:28). But no other reason stands why the impenitent ought to abstain from the Sacred Supper than that they cannot spiritually eat Christ’s Body, destitute of saving faith — while meantime equally capable of Oral Eating with Christ’s faithful disciples.
pass_b_english: SECOND genus: two hostile ‘eaters.’ Christ commanded eating and Himself ate (Matt./Mark/Luke; Fathers) — yet that He ate His own Body orally is absurd (Burmann). Spiritual eating is in John 6; Oral is deep Scripture-silence.

Spiritual mode can differ for Christ (communicating passion’s fruit) and for us (living faith). Converts in penitence are bidden; the impenitent are barred only because they cannot eat spiritually — while still as able as the faithful for Oral, if Oral were the issue (1 Cor. 11:28).
source_text: SECUNDUM Argumentorum GENUS, duplices manducantes sistit, Orali Manducationi Corporis Christi in Cœna, infensos infestósque: Ex unâ parte Christum Dominum jubentem manducare, qui & ipse manducasse, pronâ satis consequentiâ ex Matth. 26, 29. Marc. 14, 24. 25. & Luc. 22, 15. 16. colligitur, adstipulantibus Patribus, Hieronymo in Epist. ad Hedibiam Quæst. 2. August. lib. 2. de Doctrina Christiana cap. 3. Chrysostomo Hom. 83. in Matth. At Christum Corpus suum proprium, Oraliter manducasse, multis nominibus absurdum est, Vid. Burmann. Disput. XVII. de Cœna, num. 104. Dixeris: non minùs absurdum, Christum spiritualiter Corpus suum manducasse. Resp. Spiritualis manducandi Corpus Christi modus, expressè in Scriptura traditus Joh. 6. non item Oralis, de quâ altum in Scriptura silentium, manducatio licèt ipsa quà rem & absolutè, expressis verbis, in ipsâ S. Cœnæ institutione, injuncta legatur. (2) Spiritualis Corporis Christi manducandi modus, varius esse potest, alius in Christum, alius in nos competens; Non item Oralis, ubique quà rem, unus idemque, à quocunque peragatur. Christus crucifixum Corpus suum, seu crucifigendum, quatenus crucifigendum, spiritualiter manducavit, Se, passionem mortemque suam nobis communicando harumque fructum & efficaciam addicendo imputandóque; Nos Christi Corpus spiritualiter manducamus, vera vivaque fide ipsum totum cum meritis suis omnibus amplectendo, i. e. eorum participes fiendo. Ex alterâ parte, jussos manducare, h. e. ad Christianam fidem conversos, ut hinc hodieque Infideles omnes à Cœnæ S. participatione arceantur; & quidem tales Conversos ad Christianam fidem, qui seipsos probant, i. e. qui in Statu pœnitentiæ & habitu fidei vivæ consistunt, exclusis impœnitentibus & impiis. 1. Cor. 11, 28. At nulla ratio alia prostat, ob quam impœnitentes à Cœna S. abstinere debeant, quam quòd spiritualiter Corpus Christi manducare non possunt, fide salvificâ destituti, Oralis interim Manducationis cum fidelibus Christi discipulis juxta capaces.
